[h3] Warning: Spoilers! [/h3]

Not sure why I’m writing this since there are so many reviews. Just completed the game and needed to express a few thoughts about the story.

The story is so, so good. The game does a good job of making you feel like the city is real and the characters are real. I was shocked by the strength of the dialogue and voice acting. The story is a well-written novel come to life with you in the driver’s seat. The side quests add a lot too. I can’t believe how immersive games are becoming. This game really gets its hooks in you. Even after finishing everything, I was hungry for more. More story, more NPC interactions, more exploration. I’m done, but it feels like I’m not done. Like there’s more to do. Like I missed something. That’s the mark of a good game.

I was let down by the endings though. This is partly because I was expecting something like a big twist or “rug-pull” moment, as for example in Fallout 4. This is because Cyberpunk is constantly exploring the nature of existence and reality. The braindances, the idea of existing in cyberspace, cyberpsychosis, alcohol and drug use, flashbacks to the past. The fact that Johnny’s “consciousness” is replacing yours. Not to mention the game’s visual allusions to Blade Runner and the Matrix, two films that deal with the main character having some doubts about their reality. In fact, there’s an awesome detail in the last mission: when you walk up the apartment steps to the rooftop the second time, you’ll see Misty’s cat appear on the stairwell twice, like the black dejavu cat from the Matrix.

So I thought the game was heading to some crazy twist or reversal. Maybe it was all a braindance, or Johnny was not who he claimed to be, or V was not who they claimed to be. I don’t know, something. But nothing like that happens. The game plays it straight and sticks to the main plot point: removing the relic. You can choose different ways to play out this objective, and you can even give up and hand over your body to Johnny. But all the endings are the same: V gets the relic removed but has six months to live. (Or is uploaded to Mikoshi if you sided with Hanako). The only real twist, if you can call it that, is the revelation that Johnny knows he’s a copy. 

I’m not saying there always needs to be a twist or that a twist makes a story better. I do appreciate the story for what it is. I guess the reference to the dejavu cat is a meta-commentary on the player’s desire to experience the story multiple times and to effect the outcome. There’s a lot of references to fate and decision making and life paths, so maybe the point of the story is that there are some things you can’t change and just have to accept. 

Nevertheless, I’d become attached to V and was hoping for a satisfying and positive ending for both Johnny and V. Maybe in Phantom Liberty. We’ll see!

A bit of my history with this game: I didn't buy this game at launch so I don't feel burned by an early purchase. I waited until 1.5 before I jumped in. I personally had no issues with the game at that point. Then they released 2.0. It was an extremely drastic change to the game, and more than just AI behaviours. The entire skill system was completely redone and I did not like this change. It was a little too drastic in my view and caused quite a bit of frustration to me. It wasn't until after an update that broke my game and it would no longer launch. 

Support from CD Projeck Red was APAULING. In their first point of contact their first suggestion was a destructive wipe of current graphic drivers and re-installation. They didn't ask a single question about the issue, just shotgun to kill a fly. Because of their heavy handed response, I had difficulties and put me in the situation where I had to pay for someone else to fix my computer because support had wiped their hands of the issue. 

Now, here I am again, during the fight with Oda and the game is crashing again, over and over. A quick web search of this issue shows it going back for some time, and on multiple platforms, and yet, here we are, March 2024 and the problem STILL is crashing computers. Clearly this game is broken much more deeply than it would seem and it's so disheartening because there absolutely is an amazing experience if you can get it to work properly. 


Original Review:
After an incredibly infamous launch, seeing the game completely pulled from the Playstation Store for months, CD Projekt RED took a turd and turned around and made it a diamond. The game is not perfect as some issues are deep but overall the game is fun and the story is interesting and intriguing. 

I felt that choices I made were impactful enough, nothing was too deep where I was concerned I was going to ruin my game but they didn't feel superficial either. 

Customisation is done very well and I liked how they included the ability for "Vanity" wear so I can wear the best gear, but look exactly how I want. Best of both worlds. 

Skills are great and crafting different play-styles can be really fun. Being able to respec only adds to the freedom to try different builds without having to play through the entire game again. 

What really shines for me is the city. It's large and truly feels alive and breathing. Nothing seems copypasta'd and there were many times where I was driving and said, oh, this looks exactly like that other place I was only to realise I was actually in that other place after all. 

As a grumpy old man, I can recommend this game with confidence.

So this game has a lot of pros and cons.  For me, personally, the cons outweigh the pros.  Overall, the game is very Meh.  The game play is OK, and it certainly has SOME entertainment value.  I took the time to 100% it afterall.  Well let me go over some of the pros and cons.

**edit**  Bonus negative points for adding a payed DLC that included more achievements.  I 100%ed it before phantom liberty came out.

CONS

The difficulty curve is not very well laid out.  I played the game on hardest difficulty and found that the beginning was too hard and the end was too easy.  I had to play the beginning almost entirely through stealth and sneaking up on people, but by the end I could just storm through everything.  And when I say the end, I mean pretty early on.  In fact, most of the quests in the game begin to feel very quickly monotonous and a lot more like a chore than a challenge.  And I could have gone about doing it in multiple ways, whether I wanted to do it through hacking or slashing, pun intended.

And this leads to a second con...  The level cap is stupid.  Why design the game so that you can't get everything.  I understand why you can't respec as it would open up too much cheese, but preventing people from experiencing all the possibilities in one play-through is dumb.  Especially considering how repetitive the game becomes.

A third con, the story ending all kind of just plain suck in my opinion.  Like, there really is no happy ending.  There are just some that are less bad.  This, to me, just feels really not good.  If I am going to invest so much time and effort into a story and working for something, for it to end in such a shitty way kind of feels like the whole thing was just a waste of effort.  "Congratulation, you get a month of kind of happiness before you die" as the best ending is just crap.  Seriously, F that.

So when talking about story telling flaws, I have to touch on some personal pet peeves of mine.  The fact that I cannot romance the girl as a guy is just dumb.  Hear me out here.  This is a fantasy game.  A game people play to experience a fantastic or phantasmal reality.  Please, someone explain to me why anyone should be blocked the option to experience what they want to in the fantasy game.  girl on girl, guy on guy, girl on guy... why not just let them all be options?  To purposefully block a relationship option is doing nothing but pandering to the people who like that particular relationship option and blocking out people who prefer different choices.  If you want to put in gay background NPC's, sure... who cares.  Especially in this wold where people can change genitalia and reproductive systems with the sit of a chair.  like true gender swapping, not the lies that exist in the world today.  You can do that kind of stuff in a fantasy game.  So honestly, having a gay romancable NPC that limits her sexuality is actually anti woke really, as she won't even accept a gender swap as ok, because of what?  You voice hasn't changed?  The whole thing is just dumb.  In an attempt to cater to the woke mob, none of it makes sense.  And speaking of over-woke bs that annoys me, how does a "trans" character even make sense in this world.  I understand that trans issues are all over the place in our reality, but what the fuck??  This is a world where people are swapping their genders all the fucking time.  Sit in a chair for 5 minutes and get new organs.  How the fuck do trans issues even come up.  It's a FANTASY GAME.  Don't project this worlds issues into it.  Like, if it's not obvious by now, I am super anti-woke... but it's a fantasy game.  LET THE TRANS PEOPLE HAVE A WORLD WHERE THEY CAN GENDER SWAP AT WILL AND IT"S NOT A BIG CONTROVERSY???  Why project all the drama of our world into the game???  Just let people play out a fantasy.  

Honestly, who fucking goes, "I want to play a fantasy game.  In that game, I want to be bullied, harassed, and have no love partners that I like return interest in me.  Oh also, I really want the ending for the character I am role-playing as to be super shitty"  There is no grand satisfying payoff, at least story-wise, and we have this worlds drama shoved in our face.  It's unnecessary, and takes away from the goals of playing a fantasy game.

Also, all of the cars are dumb.  SO many cars, so much money, all very similar.  Buying new cars, apartments, in general was just a chore that felt overall very dissatisfying.



PROS

-Interesting skill tree... which is part of why it is so annoying that there are so many limitations on it.

-The game, at the times when the challenge level was OK, was fun.  Unfortunately most of the time it was too hard or too easy.

-It's pretty, if not a little repetitive at times



Anyway, I feel a little bad leaving a negative review since the company worked so hard to make-up for all of the games other problems it had at launch (bugs and such).  But honestly, overall, if given the chance to wipe my gameplay completely from my mind and know what I know now (like seeing this review) , I would have never played it.  So with that said, I have to mark it down.

Title: Cyberpunk 2077 - A Complex Journey Through Night City

Cyberpunk 2077, developed by CD Projekt Red, arrived with unprecedented hype and anticipation, promising a sprawling open-world RPG set in a dystopian future. As someone who eagerly awaited its release and immersed myself in Night City's neon-lit streets, I'm here to provide an in-depth review of the game.

Gameplay (3.5/5):
Cyberpunk 2077 offers an immersive and vast open world that's a playground for exploration and adventure. The ability to customize your character, enhance cyberware, and select from various skills and abilities allows for a personalized experience. The combat system offers a mix of gunplay, melee combat, and hacking, providing diverse options for approaching encounters.

However, the gameplay is a mixed bag. While some moments deliver exhilarating action and choices with meaningful consequences, others fall short. The AI can be inconsistent, and the driving mechanics leave much to be desired. Bugs and technical issues, particularly at launch, hindered the overall experience, leading to frustration.

Graphics and Sound (4.5/5):
Visually, Cyberpunk 2077 is a triumph. Night City is a breathtaking and meticulously detailed urban sprawl, with towering skyscrapers, neon signs, and a cyberpunk aesthetic that oozes style. The character models, animations, and facial expressions are impressive, lending authenticity to the game's world. The day-night cycle and weather effects further enhance the immersion.

The game's soundtrack, featuring tracks from artists like Refused and Grimes, is a standout. It complements the dystopian atmosphere and cyberpunk theme perfectly. The voice acting is generally strong, with Keanu Reeves' portrayal of Johnny Silverhand being a highlight.

Story and Worldbuilding (4/5):
The narrative in Cyberpunk 2077 is one of its strongest aspects. The main story, filled with intrigue, moral dilemmas, and memorable characters, is engaging and thought-provoking. The worldbuilding is exceptional, immersing players in a gritty and believable future where corporations wield immense power and personal identity is fluid.

Side quests and character interactions are where the game truly shines. The depth and complexity of the supporting cast add layers to the story, and the choices you make can have far-reaching consequences. Night City feels alive, with its citizens and factions contributing to the immersive experience.

Controversies and Launch Issues (2.5/5):
Cyberpunk 2077's launch was marred by numerous controversies and technical issues, especially on last-generation consoles. CD Projekt Red faced criticism for the game's performance, bugs, and missing features. While the company has since worked on patches and improvements, the initial launch left a sour taste for many players.

Conclusion (3.5/5):
Cyberpunk 2077 is a game of incredible ambition and potential, with a captivating narrative, stunning visuals, and an immersive world. However, its launch issues, technical shortcomings, and uneven gameplay experiences were disappointments for many players, including myself. The game's future may hold promise as CD Projekt Red continues to address its flaws, but as of my last knowledge update in September 2021, it remains a title that falls short of the immense expectations it carried. If you can look past the technical issues and appreciate the story and world, it still offers a unique and memorable experience, especially on more capable gaming platforms.

They've improved and changed a lot of things in 2.0, not all for the better but some of it is interesting. The game looks better, so if you cared about that, great. Unfortunately, it will run significantly less reliably.

The problem is twofold. First, and worst, a lot of the old bugs they patched out/wrote code bandaids for are back with a vengeance, and old bugs that were never exterminated are worse than ever (memory leaks, buttons and abilities not working, more memory leaks, a somehow even dumber police system where you'll be savagely beaten for doing missions for the police, more memory leaks, etc).

The second problem, and this one is basically unsolvable, is that it's still the same game. Sure, your abilities and how you influence the world is a little different, but nearly every character remains unlikeable. Now, unlikeable can be forgiven if it's done in a charismatic, interesting way - unlikeable but charismatic can be fascinating. And just like in the original release, they were hoping Keanu Fever would enthrall people.

Unfortunately his performance remains flat, lifeless, and clueless. The man doesn't even know how to pronounce low-context phrases for sh*t's sake. If Idris had been the lead from the get go, I'm guessing Cyberpunk could have been a flawed masterwork. Instead it's just flawed and boring.

You're likely to find yourself wanting to skip every drawn out, poorly conceived piece of dialogue, every care ride where you and your "partners" snipe at each other and behave like uninteresting idiot children, every "dramatic" moment where the people you're fighting are exactly as awful as you are. Whoever pitched the idea of "you'll be a dirt bag but the audience will somehow emotionally connect to you instead of every other dirtbag" must have been awfully convinced they could pull off "dirtbag we want to root for." Spoiler: they were dead wrong.

Wow what a whirlwind its been! I bought this game, hated it, came back 2.0, still didnt like it. Then, a good pal tells me to try again, he whets my appetite with a description of his wild antics in the game. I came back and finally, I was having fun. Really. I still hated the seriously weak script and paper thin narrative, I still hated V's voice and awful interjections into the story, but I was having fun! I played the game as a netrunner, I felt like the game was an rpg as I cast hacks on folks like a wizard and used my auto-target gun to take them down. I found myself finally immersed in night city, with its excellent topography and lighting. I even started to love the radio, something I initially hated. Driving in first person listening to that funky Miles Davis while dodging police was exceptional. However, as I continued the assault side missions, they all blended into one. I became so powerful as a net runner the game no longer had any sort of challenge. I was walking into enemy encampments and killing everyone with my hacks, it all felt pointless. Essentially, Cyberpunk has a soul problem. Much like the robots in the game, this game has no soul. It is a 7/10 with a pretty face with no soul to bear. The game tricks you into thinking you have agency over its awful narrative, and the game also makes you feel like your on a real RPG power path. This identity crisis hurts the game in my opinion, leaving  the player bored and exhausted from seeing the same mission play out, again and again and again and again. Oh well. Even though its a 7/10 I still give this one a bad review, because it had the potential to be so much more.

CyberPunk 2.0

I loved the original cyber punk upon release even with it's bugs. I don't know why they would regress a great system instead of just enhancing what they already had to make it better.

Level scaling:
Enemies now match your level no matter where you go. I don't completely hate it, but I don't love it either. It's just artificial difficulty to make people play longer. We already had difficulty levels, why add artificial difficulty? Also you made an RPG game, why are you introducing a system that defeats the purpose of RPGs and getting stronger in the first place? Characters are supposed to feel overpowered. If anything it should have been optional.

DLSS 3.5:
does absolutely nothing for older cards. I was hoping to hope on and gain at least 15% FPS with a 2080TI and ray tracing on. I actually lost 15% FPS when it's turned on. Basically useless feature. and no, I don't have path tracing on, I fixed the bug where you can't enable it without path tracing on.

New Skill Tree:
My biggest problem is the new skill tree. Complete garbage compared to the old system. I am playing around with the new build planner linked below and immediately can tell how very limited it is in customization. You used to be able to run some pretty cool builds like poison damage through cyber hacks and gain crit on poison and poison damage increase through mixing up intelligence with cool. Now you can't do any of that at all. All of the trees are very specific like "SMGs only" or "throwable weapons only". What if I want the extra headshot damage or crit damage from a cyber hack?

I mean what were they thinking, the skill tree has lost all complexity for a brain dead bare bones system. They should have kept all the weapon trees separated like they used to have them which allowed you to get some cool buffs off other trees that had nothing to do with the weapon you're using.

Oh and the relic system? It's just basic stuff they could have added to the normal skill tree. There's no hybrid mechanics offered at all that could have brought the opportunity for more advanced builds. What they should have done is made the relic system where you can select an advanced class that compliments your current build. There's no complexity to it at all. Unexciting and boring.

I can forgive the enemy level scaling and even the DLSS because it's newer technology. I however can not forgive the over simplification of the skill tree to the point where a monkey can literally slam keys to come up with a build and it wouldn't make much of a difference.

The rest of this review is just gonna be a long list of complaints about controls, because the controls in this game are just fucking abysmal. 
A mod is required to rebind half the keybinds, including secondary interact. 
Several actions cancel hold-to-sprint. Walking down stairs, jumping, sliding, or walking into a wall. If you continue to hold the sprint button through these actions, it won't continue your sprint. Similar situation with acceleration on driving. 
You can sprint up stairs, but not down them. If you let go of sprint mid-air, then immediately press it again, you will sprint when you land. I can't imagine the thought process behind making it so awkward to just sprint.
With the 2.0 update, W/S navigate the UI and text prompts. Meaning, if you're on the phone while walking, W will scroll through your prompts. And that one's hardcoded, can't be changed even with the mod. No multitasking for you.
If someone is talking to you and the "Skip ahead" prompt is available, you will not be able to crouch. Meaning if you're on a mission with another NPC that's talking to you, and you're trying to stealth, you can't. You either don't crouch, or you just wait till they stop talking.

If you don't wanna use CDPR's special curated keybinds, then it's just one massive QOL nightmare.
